newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open up 7.00 to 10.00 cents.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open up 7.00 to 10.00 cents.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open up 7.00 to 10.00 cents Wednesday after a monthly report showed a much lower-than-expected rise in consumer coffee stocks, traders said.
Supplies of green coffee stored in U.S. warehouses rose in March by 111,000 60-kg bags, to 1,657,000 bags, Green Coffee Association of New York reported after the close on Tuesday.
Most analysts had forecast an increase of between 250,000 and 300,000 bags, with some operators looking for a build of up to 700,000 bags.

"People thought the stocks were going to be up much more," one trader said. But he remained cautious, saying the GCA data may not prove to be as bullish as some people expect. "It's not enough for me to believe the market's going to open 10.00 higher. I'll believe it when I see it."

Tuesday, New York arabica futures erased early gains and finished mainly lower as operators anticipated a sharp build in U.S. stockpiles. May delivery ended down 3.60 cents at 192.40 cents a lb after trading from 201.50 to 191.00. Second-month July settled 2.35 cents lower.
The May/July switch, a barometer of nearby availability, narrowed to 17.75 cents, up from 19.00 cents at the close on Friday.
Technically, traders pegged May near-term resistance at 202.00 cents, with the next upside objective seen at 205.00 cents. They pegged May support at 190.00 cents, then 187.00 cents.
On the fundamental side, Brazilian stevedores will go on national strike in sympathy with Santos port workers at midnight Thursday (0300 GMT Friday) for 48 hours, a union official said.

Stevedores at Santos began an indefinite strike on Tuesday in protest against steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) using its own workers to load and unload vessels at its private terminal at the port.
After Tuesday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks were unchanged, at 80,828 60-kg bags as of April 14. There were no bags pending grading, the exchange said.
London robusta prices were sharply higher after a weak start Wednesday, buoyed by the GCA stock data. LIFFE May was up $52 at the midday break, to $1,630 a tonne, while July rose $60, to $1,655.
